text: “I thought you were a ghost or a dream,” he said. “You can’t bite a ghost or a dream, and if you scream they don’t care.” “Would you hate it if—if a boy looked at you?” Mary asked uncertainly. He lay back on his cushion and paused thoughtfully. “There’s one boy,” he said quite slowly, as if he were thinking over every word, “there’s one boy I believe I shouldn’t mind. It’s that boy who knows where the foxes live—Dickon.” “I’m sure you wouldn’t mind him,” said Mary.
